pumac-2010-algebra-a-01.title: Plug in x = 1
pumac-2010-algebra-a-01.body:
The sum of the coefficients of $f(x)$ is $f(1)$. Here $f(1)=(63-61)^4=2^4=16$.

**Answer: 16**

pumac-2010-algebra-a-05.title: Build the polynomial with roots 1/(root - 2)
pumac-2010-algebra-a-05.body:
The numbers $\alpha-2,\beta-2,\gamma-2$ are the roots of $g(x)=f(x+2)=3x^3+13x^2+18x+2$. The reciprocals $y_i=\frac1{\alpha_i-2}$ are the roots of the reversed polynomial $h(y)=2y^3+18y^2+13y+3$.

By Vieta, $y_1+y_2+y_3=-\frac{18}2=-9$ and $y_1y_2+y_2y_3+y_3y_1=\frac{13}2$. Therefore
$$\sum y_i^2=\Big(\sum y_i\Big)^2-2\sum y_iy_j=81-13=68.$$

**Answer: 68**

pumac-2010-algebra-a-08.title: Use divisibility of values
pumac-2010-algebra-a-08.body:
If $p(n)=n+82$ then $x-n$ divides $p(x)-x-82$ as a polynomial with integer coefficients, so for every integer $a$, $a-n$ divides $p(a)-a-82$.

Thus $15-n\mid p(15)-15-82=-91$ and $35-n\mid p(35)-35-82=-91$. So $15-n$ and $35-n$ are divisors of $91$ (among $\pm1,\pm7,\pm13,\pm91$) that differ by $20$. The only possibilities are $(15-n,35-n)=(-13,7)$ giving $n=28$, or $(-7,13)$ giving $n=22$.

But $n=22$ is impossible because $p(22)=1196\neq22+82$. So $n=28$.

**Answer: 28**
